newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan labour leader bows to peoples' verdict.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan labour leader bows to peoples' verdict.

text.p: A Sri Lankan cabinet minister whose supporters deserted him at recent local elections said on Sunday he accepted the verdict as a message to change his political strategy.

"This is a fine demonstration by my people that they desire a change," said Savumiamoorthy Thondaman, Minister of Rural Industries and leader of the Ceylon Workers' Congress (CWC), the island's biggest plantations labour union.
"I have accepted their message," he told a news conference. "I plan to reorganise the movement."

CWC members defied Thondaman's call to support the ruling People's Alliance (PA) government at the March 21 poll and voted for the opposition United National Party (UNP), which they backed for 17 years until it was ousted by the PA in 1994.
The CWC has secured wage increases in the past by threatening strikes which could badly disrupt the plantations industry, traditionally the bedrock of Sri Lanka's economy.

The union, made up mainly of minority Tamil estate workers of Indian origin, is politically powerful because Thondaman has used its estimated 400,000 members as a bloc vote to help either of the two main political parties at elections.

The PA swept to a landslide victory in the local poll, winning 194 of the 238 local bodies at stake. The UNP won only 43, mainly in the central hills where large numbers of Tamils work on tea estates.
Thondaman, who was a UNP cabinet minister before he switched allegiances after its 1994 defeat, said he had no intention of resigning his portfolio.
Industry analysts have said estate workers were dissatisfied with the CWC leadership and confused by Thondaman's political opportunism.
The CWC is currently nearing a deal on a collective agreement with management firms running Sri Lanka's tea, rubber and coconut plantations.
Management firms already have a deal with the union to freeze wages up to December 1997, as a prelude to the collective agreement.
